---
title: "Contributing"
---

Thank you for your interest in contributing to draggg! This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to the project.

## Getting Started

1. **Fork the repository** on GitHub
2. **Clone your fork:**
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/your-username/draggg.git
   cd draggg
   ```

3. **Set up development environment:**
   ```bash
   python3 -m venv venv
   source venv/bin/activate
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

4. **Create a branch for your work:**
   ```bash
   git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
   # or
   git checkout -b fix/your-bug-fix
   ```

## Development Workflow

### Code Style

- Follow **PEP 8** Python style guidelines
- Use **type hints** for all function signatures
- Include **docstrings** for all classes and functions
- Keep lines under 100 characters when possible
- Use meaningful variable and function names

### Testing

- Write tests for new features
- Test on your target platform before submitting PR
- Include test results in your PR description

### Documentation

- Update relevant documentation when adding features
- Update README.md if installation or usage changes
- Add docstrings to new functions and classes
- Update CHANGELOG.md for user-facing changes

## Areas for Contribution

We welcome contributions in these areas:

- **Additional touchpad driver support**
- **Wayland improvements**
- **Gesture customization**
- **Performance optimizations**
- **Additional gesture types**
- **Multi-platform support** (macOS and Windows)
- **Documentation improvements**
- **Bug fixes**

## Submitting Changes

1. **Commit your changes:**
   ```bash
   git add .
   git commit -m "Description of your changes"
   ```

2. **Push to your fork:**
   ```bash
   git push origin feature/your-feature-name
   ```

3. **Create a Pull Request** on GitHub

4. **Describe your changes** in the PR:
   - What changed and why
   - How to test the changes
   - Any breaking changes

## Code Review Process

- All PRs require review before merging
- Address review comments promptly
- Keep PRs focused on a single feature or fix
- Update documentation as needed

## Questions?

Feel free to open an issue on GitHub if you have questions about contributing!
